issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: Poolable / Resettable CBOR Readers
issue_context.body:
### Background and motivation

Today, `CborReader` is a "one-shot" type that must be discarded after it has finished reading the buffer it was created with. Internally the reader allocates multiple collections for bookeeping. If you are reading multiple CBOR documents in a hot loop, this can generate a lot of garbage. 

It would be desirable to be able to "reset" the `CborReader` and provide it a new buffer to reuse the resources more efficently. This would also allow readers to be pooled. It should also be noted that `CborWriter` already includes a `Reset()` API.

My real-world use case is a database that stores many small (100-300 bytes) documents using CBOR. The overhead of allocating new readers for each "row", is a key performance concern. There is also a need to be able to incrementally read [CBOR Sequences](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/[draft-ietf-cbor-sequence-02](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-cbor-sequence-02)) which may consist of many concatenated CBOR documents. (Although this might need additional APIs to cope with buffer boundaries truncating CBOR documents).


@-ing prior CBOR API proposer and reviewers, apologies if this is improper.

@eiriktsarpalis @bartonjs @terrajobst 


### API Proposal [version 2]

```diff
namespace System.Formats.Cbor;

public CborReader
{
//resets reader state
+ void Reset(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> data);
}
```

### API Usage

### Reset
The Reset API will reset all internal state to a condition identical to calling `new CborReader(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, ...)`, including removing any references to the previous `data` buffer. This also includes any exceptional state.

NOTE : It is explicitly **valid** to call either the existing ctor `new CborReader(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, ...)` OR the proposed `Reset(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>)`  with an empty/default `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`. However, any calls to  `Read*`, `Skip*` or `Peek*` APIs will fail since there is no valid CBOR document.


### Alternative Designs

_No response_

### Risks

### Background and motivation Today, `CborReader` is a "one-shot" type that must be discarded after it has finished reading the buffer it was created with. Internally the reader allocates multiple collections for bookeeping. If you are reading multiple CBOR documents in a hot loop, this can generate a lot of garbage. It would be desirable to be able to "reset" the `CborReader` and provide it a new buffer to reuse the resources more efficently. This would also allow readers to be pooled. It should also be noted that `CborWriter` already includes a `Reset()` API. My real-world use case is a database that stores many small (100-300 bytes) documents using CBOR. The overhead of allocating new readers for each "row", is a key performance concern. There is also a need to be able to incrementally read [CBOR Sequences](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/[draft-ietf-cbor-sequence-02](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-cbor-sequence-02)) which may consist of many concatenated CBOR documents. (Although this might need additional APIs to cope with buffer boundaries truncating CBOR documents). @-ing prior CBOR API proposer and reviewers, apologies if this is improper. @eiriktsarpalis @bartonjs @terrajobst ### API Proposal ```diff namespace System.Formats.Cbor; public CborReader { //Allow creation of empty reader + CborReader(CborConformanceMode conformanceMode = CborConformanceMode.Strict, bool allowMultipleRootLevelValues = false); //removes reference to `data` buffer and resets reader state + void Reset(); //optional API, may be more trouble than it is worth + void Reset(CborConformanceMode conformanceMode = CborConformanceMode.Strict, bool allowMultipleRootLevelValues = false); //sets the internal buffer, making an empty/rested reader ready to use. + void SetBuffer(ReadOnlyMemory data); } ``` ### API Usage ### Constructor The changes allow you to create a `CborReader` with no buffer. In this state, calling any `Read*`, `Skip*` or `Peek*` method will result in an `InvalidOperationException`. The existing ctor would remain as the normal way to create a ready-to-use reader. ### Reset The Reset API will reset all internal state to a condition identical to calling `new CborReader()`, including removing any references to the `data` buffer. This also includes any exceptional state After Reset has been called, as with the new ctor, calling any `Read*`, `Skip*` or `Peek*` method will result in an `InvalidOperationException` until `SetBuffer()` has been called with a valid buffer. ### SetBuffer The `SetBuffer()` method will set the internal data buffer and move the reader into a usable state ready for consumption. #### Primary Design If the intenal buffer has already been set, `SetBuffer()` will internally call `Reset()`, clobbering the internal state. #### Alternative Design As an API alternative, calling `SetBuffer()` multiple times without interleaving a `Reset()` call would result in an `InvalidOperationException` ### Alternative Designs _No response_ ### Risks - All `Read*`, `Skip*` or `Peek*` APIs will incur a check to ensure `_data` is valid, adding to overhead. - There is an increased risk of invalid use of the APIs or developer confusion.

Also, so far as I can tell: Congratulations on having the first feature request to the System.Formats.Cbor library :smile:

> A much simpler variant seems to be just to add

I should have included that in my initial proposal.

I had a thought that separating the `SetBuffer` and `Reset` calls would allow object pools to wipe state. But maybe that doesn't matter. An object pool could in theory call `Reset` with an empty ROM and that could be valid as long as the reader doesn't advance on it.
I gather this probably won't make it for .NET 7?
Presumably not? I'm not sure how to move an issue toward API Review. I'd be willing to implement it if the API is approved.
